title: Count Directed Walks of Exact Length K
description: You are given a directed graph with `n` vertices labeled `0` to `n - 1` and a list of directed edges `edges` where each entry `[u, v]` represents a directed edge from `u` to `v` (self-loops and parallel edges are allowed and count as distinct edges). Given source `src`, destination `dst`, and a non-negative 64-bit integer `k`, return the number of distinct directed walks of exact length `k` from `src` to `dst`, modulo `10^9 + 7`.
hints: Construct the `n x n` adjacency matrix `A` where `A[u][v]` counts the number of directed edges from `u` to `v`.
The entry `(A^k)[src][dst]` equals the exact number of walks of length `k` from `src` to `dst`; compute `A^k mod (10^9 + 7)` using binary matrix exponentiation in O(n^3 log k) time.

examples.explanation: The only walk of length 2 from 0 to 2 is 0 -> 1 -> 2, giving 1.
The 3 walks of length 3 from 0 to 0 are 0-0-0-0, 0-0-1-0, and 0-1-0-0.
A walk of length 0 starts and ends at the same vertex, so src == dst gives 1.
